summary: The paper studies discrete mean-variance portfolio optimisation with 8 assets encoded in 16 qubits, comparing QAOA, QAOAz, and QWOA over p=1 to 19. For n=8 and A=4, the reported search spaces are 65,536 for QAOA, 12,870 for QAOAz, and 66 for QWOA; QWOA reaches over 40% optimal-portfolio probability on Data Set A and about 20% on Data Set B, while QAOA has the largest objective-value variance (12.96 on Data Set A) and QAOAz remains below 10^-9/10^-6 on the optimal state in the highlighted bands.

experiments.description: Numerical simulation of portfolio optimisation using QAOA, QAOAz, and QWOA on two real-market datasets, comparing expected portfolio quality, return, and risk as a function of circuit depth p.

algorithm.variant: QAOA, QAOAz (Quantum Alternating Operator Ansatz), and QWOA (Quantum Walk Optimisation Algorithm)
algorithm.parameter_initialization: random uniform [0, 2π] for all variational parameters

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Two qubits per asset encode three asset positions: |01⟩ long, |10⟩ short, |00⟩ or |11⟩ no position (degenerate in QAOA/QAOAz; QWOA restricts to canonical non-degenerate valid states).
problem_formulation.objective_function: c(z) = λ Σ_{i,j=1}^n σ_{ij} z_i z_j - (1-λ) Σ_{i=1}^n r_i z_i, subject to Σ_i z_i = A
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: QAOA uses penalty term ζ(z)=ϵ(A-Σ_i z_i)^2; QAOAz uses dual-parity-ring mixer preserving constraint subspace; QWOA uses indexing over valid non-degenerate solutions and quantum walk mixer on complete graph over feasible states.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: C diagonal in computational basis with entries c(z) (and c(z)+ζ(z) for QAOA)

problem_instance.description: Discrete mean-variance Markowitz portfolio optimisation with 8 assets and net position constraint A=4.
problem_instance.dataset_name: Data Set A; Data Set B

dataset_specification.description: Data Set A: AMP, ANZ, AMC, BHP, BXB, CBA, CSL, IAG from 01/01/2017 to 31/12/2018. Data Set B: FLT, QAN, WEB, REX, AIZ, SYD, SCG, CTD from 24/03/2020 to 06/09/2020.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Adjusted close prices from Yahoo Finance; used to account for corporate actions such as dividends.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 15 independent repeats per algorithm per dataset; same randomly generated initial parameters used across methods; results reported as mean and standard deviation versus p.

implementation_details.classical_solver: BFGS; Newton-Conjugate-Gradient, Nelder-Mead Simplex, and Powell’s method also considered as alternatives
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Historical price data used to compute expected returns and covariances; objective and constraint parameters set to λ=0.5 and A=4.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measured/optimized expectation values converted to expected annual return and risk; brute-force classical search used to identify minimum objective value for comparison.

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: QWOA improves rapidly with p; QAOAz shows diminishing improvement past p≈8; QAOA performs worst and has largest variance

speedup_claims.factor: QWOA search space reduced to 0.406% of QAOA and 14.61% of QAOAz
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a search-space reduction, not an end-to-end runtime speedup; QWOA has higher per-iteration mixing complexity (O(n^2)).

speedup_claims.factor: QWOA search space scales as M(n,A), approximately 3^n/(2 sqrt(pi n)) for A = 0; QAOA scales as 4^n and QAOAz as 4^n/sqrt(pi n)
speedup_claims.conditions: asymptotic scaling discussion in the paper
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper presents asymptotic search-space scaling, not a proven computational speedup.

speedup_claims.factor: QWOA reaches ~40% probability on the optimal portfolio for Data Set A and ~20% for Data Set B
speedup_claims.caveats: Probability amplification is shown in simulation; no hardware experiment is reported.

speedup_claims.factor: QAOAz optimal-state probability remains below 10^-9 (Data Set A) and 10^-6 (Data Set B)
speedup_claims.conditions: at p = 19, in the relevant parity band containing the optimal solution
speedup_claims.caveats: This reflects degeneracy and disconnected parity bands in QAOAz.

speedup_claims.factor: QWOA mixer complexity O(n^2) versus QAOA/QAOAz O(n) per iteration
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper argues the search-space reduction outweighs the polynomial increase in circuit depth.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: QAOA O(n), QAOAz O(n), QWOA O(n^2) per the paper’s gate-complexity discussion; search spaces: 2^(2n), binomial(2n, n+A), and M(n,A) respectively
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Brute-force over feasible solutions for comparison; exact asymptotic complexity not stated

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established; only p up to 19 on n=8 assets is reported, with no end-to-end classical runtime crossover analysis.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require scalable fault-tolerant hardware and a classical baseline comparison at larger n; the paper only reports noiseless numerical simulation and brute-force reference minima.
limiting_factors: Problem size is small (n=8 assets, 16 qubits)
Classical brute-force baseline is only used for reference minima, not as a full runtime comparison

notes: hardware.type inferred as simulator_other because the paper reports numerical simulation using QuOP MPI and no real QPU device.
num_qubits inferred from 2 qubits per asset and n=8 assets, giving 16 qubits.

speedup_order inferred as none_proven because the paper reports improved empirical performance and circuit/search-space comparisons but no asymptotic end-to-end quantum speedup over the best classical method.
The paper reports improved empirical performance of QWOA over QAOA and QAOAz, but only in noiseless numerical simulation on a small portfolio instance.
No practical quantum advantage over classical methods is demonstrated.

experiments.description: QAOA portfolio optimisation on the same two datasets, using a soft constraint penalty and full 2^(2n) search space.
key_results: Maximum standard deviation of objective value 12.96 on Data Set A
Performs worst among the three methods on both datasets

experiments.description: QAOAz portfolio optimisation using the dual-parity-ring mixer that preserves the constraint subspace but leaves disconnected parity bands.
key_results: Maximum standard deviation of objective value 0.038 on Data Set A and 0.61 on Data Set B
Optimal solution probability remains below 10^-9 on Data Set A and 10^-6 on Data Set B

experiments.description: QWOA portfolio optimisation using indexing over valid non-degenerate solutions and a complete-graph quantum walk mixer.
key_results: Maximum standard deviation of objective value 0.011 on Data Set A and 0.115 on Data Set B
Optimal solution probability reaches over 40% on Data Set A and about 20% on Data Set B
